description: Codified local knowledge about macOS disk hogs and how to reclaim them. safety: 'safe' = regenerated automatically, 'caution' = you lose something you may want back (re-download / rebuild cost), 'manual' = needs a human decision.

rules.title: Trash
rules.why: Files you already deleted. Space is not returned until the Trash is emptied.
rules.note: Check the contents first; this is the last stop before the bytes are gone.

rules.title: Xcode DerivedData
rules.why: Build intermediates, indexes and module caches. Rebuilt automatically on the next build.
rules.note: Quit Xcode first. First build afterwards is slow.

rules.title: Xcode iOS DeviceSupport
rules.why: Symbols for every iOS version you ever attached a device with. Re-downloaded on demand.

rules.title: Xcode Archives
rules.why: Shipped build archives with dSYMs. Needed to symbolicate crash reports for released versions.
rules.note: Keep archives for any build still in the wild; you cannot symbolicate its crashes without them.

rules.title: iOS Simulator devices
rules.why: Each simulator device is a full disk image with its own apps and data.
rules.note: 'delete unavailable' only removes devices for runtimes you no longer have. 'xcrun simctl erase all' wipes data from all simulators.

rules.title: CoreSimulator caches
rules.why: Cached simulator runtimes and dyld caches. Regenerated.

rules.title: node_modules directories
rules.why: Reinstallable from the lockfile with npm/yarn/pnpm install.
rules.note: Only suggested for projects untouched for 90+ days. Requires network to restore.

rules.title: Build output directories
rules.why: Compiler output. Regenerated by the next build.
rules.note: 'target' is Rust/Maven; 'Pods' restores with pod install.

rules.title: Python virtualenvs
rules.why: Recreatable from requirements.txt / pyproject.toml.
rules.note: Only safe if the project actually pins its dependencies.

rules.title: npm cache
rules.why: Downloaded package tarballs. Purely a network-time optimisation.

rules.title: yarn / pnpm / bun caches
rules.why: Package download caches.
rules.note: pnpm's store is hard-linked into node_modules; clearing it forces re-download. Prefer 'pnpm store prune'.

rules.title: Cargo registry & git checkouts
rules.why: Downloaded crate sources. Re-fetched on next build.

rules.title: Go module cache
rules.why: Downloaded modules and build cache.
rules.note: Module cache files are read-only; use 'go clean' rather than rm.

rules.title: Gradle / Maven caches
rules.why: Downloaded JARs and build caches.

rules.title: Homebrew downloads
rules.why: Downloaded bottles and old installed versions.

rules.title: Docker Desktop VM disk image
rules.why: One sparse file holding every image, container and volume. Frequently the single largest file on a developer Mac.
rules.note: Deleting the .raw destroys all images and volumes. Prune first; the file only shrinks after Docker Desktop reclaims space (Settings > Resources > Disk image size).

rules.title: OrbStack data
rules.why: OrbStack VM and container storage.

rules.title: VS Code / Cursor caches
rules.why: Editor caches, cached extension data and old workspace state.

rules.title: Editor-managed Node/npx cache
rules.why: Zed and similar editors run language servers and MCP servers via npx, and each invocation caches a full node_modules tree under the editor's support directory. These accumulate indefinitely and nothing prunes them.
rules.note: Re-downloaded on next use. Quit the editor first.

rules.title: App-bundled VM images & sandboxes
rules.why: Some desktop apps ship a Linux VM rootfs for sandboxed execution. Usually sparse, often several GB, and rebuilt on demand.
rules.note: Removing forces the app to re-provision its VM on next launch, which needs network and time.

rules.title: Superseded app versions
rules.why: Self-updating apps keep previous versions side by side; only the newest is used.
rules.note: Keep the highest version number; remove older siblings.

rules.title: Per-user temp & cache (/private/var/folders)
rules.why: DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR: app update stagings, Chrome framework copies, temp files. Cleared on reboot in part, but large items persist.
rules.note: Quit the owning app first; some entries are live temp files.

rules.title: Messaging app attachments
rules.why: Signal/WhatsApp/Telegram store every received photo and video locally.
rules.note: Use the app's own storage settings; deleting files directly can corrupt its database.

rules.title: Sleep image
rules.why: RAM contents written to disk for hibernation; sized to your installed RAM.
rules.note: Recreated automatically. Only worth disabling (pmset hibernatemode 0) on a desktop; on a laptop it protects against data loss on battery exhaustion.

rules.title: iCloud Drive local copies
rules.why: Files synced from iCloud that are also stored locally.
rules.note: Requires Full Disk Access to measure. Free space with Finder > right-click > Remove Download, or enable Optimise Mac Storage.

rules.title: ~/Library/Caches entries
rules.why: Per-application caches. Apps recreate what they need.
rules.note: Mostly safe, but some apps keep real data here (e.g. downloaded model weights). Check what it is before clearing.

rules.title: Sandboxed app caches
rules.why: Caches inside App Store / sandboxed app containers.

rules.title: ~/.cache
rules.why: XDG-style cache directory used by many CLI tools.

rules.title: Hugging Face model cache
rules.why: Downloaded model weights. Re-downloadable but often tens of GB and slow to refetch.
rules.note: Use 'huggingface-cli delete-cache' to prune selectively rather than nuking everything.

rules.title: Ollama models
rules.why: Local LLM weights, several GB each.
rules.note: List with 'ollama list', remove individually with 'ollama rm <model>'.

rules.title: iOS device backups
rules.why: Full local backups of iPhone/iPad. Often 50 GB+ and easily forgotten.
rules.note: Manage in Finder > device > Manage Backups. Do not delete the only backup of a device you still own.

rules.title: Mail attachments & downloads
rules.why: Locally cached message bodies and attachments.
rules.note: In Mail: Settings > Accounts > Download Attachments = None, then remove the account's local cache.

rules.title: Photos library
rules.why: Usually the biggest single item on a personal Mac.
rules.note: Enable 'Optimise Mac Storage' in Photos settings, and empty Photos > Recently Deleted.

rules.title: Music / Podcasts media
rules.why: Downloaded tracks and podcast episodes.

rules.title: Stale Downloads
rules.why: Installers and archives you already used.

rules.title: Large disk images & installers
rules.why: DMG/ISO/IPSW/PKG files are rarely needed after install.

rules.title: iOS firmware images (.ipsw)
rules.why: Device firmware, ~7 GB each, re-downloadable from Apple.

rules.title: Logs & diagnostic reports
rules.why: Application logs and crash reports.

rules.title: Browser caches & service workers
rules.why: Web caches; rebuilt as you browse.
rules.note: Quit the browser first or it will just rewrite them.

rules.title: Adobe media cache
rules.why: Peak/conformed audio and video cache files.

rules.title: Steam / game libraries
rules.why: Installed games are re-downloadable.

rules.title: Old language toolchains
rules.why: Installed interpreter/SDK versions you may no longer use.
rules.note: Check which ones are referenced by .python-version / .nvmrc files before removing.

rules.title: APFS local snapshots
rules.why: Time Machine keeps local snapshots that pin the blocks of deleted files. This is the usual reason deleting files frees nothing.
rules.note: Reported by 'spacefinder overview', not by the file scan -- snapshots are invisible to a directory walk.
